solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Many shops endlessly supplying tea

indicators.note: endlessly says the final letter of the word for many shops is cut off

parts.note: a chain is a group of shops under one owner

explanation.surface: A chain of stores that sells tea everywhere, without end.
explanation.definitionFit: Chai is the Hindi word for tea, now common in English for spiced tea.

clue.text: Hard working, in terms of judges

definitions.meaning: difficult or wearing, as a hard day is
judges at work are hearing cases, putting defendants on trial

explanation.surface: Judges' work described as hard going.
explanation.definitionFit: A trying task is a difficult one, and judges at work are busy trying cases in court.

clue.text: Orchestral component supporting piano with skill

indicators.note: in a down answer a piece that supports another sits beneath it

parts.note: P is the musical abbreviation for piano, softly
art means skill, as in the art of persuasion

explanation.surface: A section of the orchestra backing up the pianist with skill.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'supporting' puts ART below P.
explanation.definitionFit: Each instrument in an orchestra plays its own written line of the score, called its part.

clue.text: A degree of latitude is right in subject

indicators.note: in says the letter for right goes inside the word for subject

parts.note: a topic is a subject of discussion

explanation.surface: Whether a bit of geographical latitude is the right topic to discuss.
explanation.definitionFit: The tropics of Cancer and Capricorn are lines at about 23.5 degrees of latitude north and south.

clue.text: Artist is able in translation to deliver French writer

parts.note: RA, Royal Academician, stands for an artist

indicators.note: translation turns words into another form, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A painter who can translate, producing a French author's work.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in translation' rearranges IS ABLE into BELAIS, which follows RA.
explanation.definitionFit: François Rabelais was the sixteenth-century French author of Gargantua and Pantagruel.

clue.text: Agitated President buttonholing a person in the street

indicators.note: to buttonhole is to waylay and hold someone, so the shuffled letters hold the a
agitated means stirred up, so these letters are shaken into a new order

explanation.surface: A worked-up head of state collaring a passer-by.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Agitated' shuffles PRESIDENT and 'buttonholing' puts A inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: A walker on the street is a pedestrian, someone travelling on foot.

clue.text: Tea is only half-brewed? It may impress some

parts.note: char is an informal British word for tea

indicators.note: only half says just the first two of four letters are used

parts.note: in northern English to mash tea is to brew it

explanation.surface: A disappointing cuppa that has only half brewed; perhaps some are impressed anyway.
explanation.walkthrough: MASH is a dialect word for brewing tea; half of it gives MA.
explanation.definitionFit: Charisma is a compelling personal charm that wins over and impresses many people.

clue.text: Jug with wine given a shake

parts.note: jug and stir are both slang for prison
red is wine of that colour

explanation.surface: A jug of wine being shaken up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Jug' is slang for prison here, as is STIR.
explanation.definitionFit: To stir something is to mix it by moving it about, much as shaking does.

clue.text: Academic back to suppress revolution in education

indicators.note: to suppress is to hold down, so the reversed letters are held inside

parts.note: the rear is the back

indicators.note: revolution turns the abbreviation for education around

explanation.surface: An academic returning to crush a revolt in schools.
explanation.walkthrough: 'revolution in' turns ED to DE, and 'to suppress' puts DE inside REAR.
explanation.definitionFit: In British universities a reader is a senior academic ranking just below professor.

clue.text: Book Two covering family — it provides little coverage of the individual

definitions.text: it provides little coverage of the individual

indicators.note: covering means wrapping around, so the Roman two goes round the family word

parts.note: II is two in Roman numerals
kin are one's family

explanation.surface: A second volume dealing with family, then a dig at skimpy swimwear.
explanation.walkthrough: 'covering' puts KIN inside II.
explanation.definitionFit: A two-piece swimsuit famously skimpy, covering very little of the wearer's body.

clue.text: Tense examination once securing power for senior people?

parts.note: T is the grammar abbreviation for tense

indicators.note: securing means holding fast, so the old exam encloses the letter for power

parts.note: O level was the British school exam replaced by GCSE in 1988
P is the physics symbol for power

explanation.surface: A nervous sitting of an old-style exam that hands power to the senior people.
explanation.walkthrough: O LEVEL was a British school exam taken at about 16 until 1988.
explanation.definitionFit: Top-level describes the highest rank, involving the most senior officials.

clue.text: Organ teaching possibly involves source of religious music in church

indicators.note: involves means takes in, so the shuffled letters take in the first letter
possibly signals the letters could be set out another way
the source of a word is its opening letter

explanation.surface: Organ lessons that perhaps take in the roots of church music.
explanation.walkthrough: 'possibly' rearranges ORGAN TEACHING and 'involves' takes in R, the 'source of religious'.
explanation.definitionFit: Plainsong named after Pope Gregory I, sung in unison in Catholic liturgy.

clue.text: Most uncommon to receive data identifying location of habitat loss

indicators.note: to receive is to take in, so the word for most uncommon takes in the data

parts.note: rarest means most uncommon
info is short for information, data

explanation.surface: The rarest species are being tracked using data that pinpoints where habitats are disappearing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to receive' puts INFO inside RAREST, splitting it RA-REST.
explanation.definitionFit: Tropical forest being felled is the classic case of wildlife habitat destruction.

clue.text: Tea service upset after end of tea

indicators.note: after says the reversed word comes behind the single letter
the end of a word is its last letter
upset in a down answer turns the word upside down, reading it backwards

parts.note: a mass is a church service

explanation.surface: A tea service knocked over once the tea was finished.
explanation.walkthrough: 'upset' turns MASS into SSAM, which comes 'after' A, the 'end of tea'.
explanation.definitionFit: A strong black tea grown in the Indian state of the same name.

clue.text: Seizes head of partner in crime, making retreat

indicators.note: retreat means go back, so the assembled letters are read backwards
in puts the first letter inside the word for crime

parts.note: sin means wrongdoing, a crime

indicators.note: the head of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: Grabbing the leader of an accomplice in crime and fleeing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' puts P into SIN to make SPIN, and 'making retreat' turns that backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: To nip is to pinch or grab sharply, so seizes is a fair synonym.

clue.text: Water creature near, circling river area

indicators.note: circling means going round, so the mean word surrounds the two letters

parts.note: near is old-fashioned British slang for stingy, mean with money

explanation.surface: A sea creature close by, circling a stretch of river.
explanation.walkthrough: 'near' here means mean with money, not close.
explanation.definitionFit: A flat fish with a venomous barbed tail that lives in seas and rivers.

clue.text: Ancient tax covering last of transactions

indicators.note: covering means wrapping around, so the tax word goes round the letter

parts.note: a duty is a tax on goods

indicators.note: the last of a word is its final letter

explanation.surface: An old levy charged on the final deal.
explanation.definitionFit: Something dusty is old and neglected, so it suggests great age.

clue.text: Amateur handiwork overturned something attractive leading to language

indicators.note: overturned in a down answer turns the word upside down, reading it backwards

parts.note: DIY, do-it-yourself, is home handiwork by amateurs
a dish is slang for an attractive person

explanation.surface: A botched home repair knocked over, and something appealing leads to a new language.
explanation.walkthrough: 'overturned' turns DIY to YID; DISH is slang for an attractive person.
explanation.definitionFit: The Germanic language of Ashkenazi Jews, written in Hebrew script.

clue.text: Political discourse a little lacking in character

indicators.note: a little lacking says a small bit, the final letter, is missing

parts.note: spine means strength of character, backbone

explanation.surface: Talk among politicians that is somewhat short on integrity.
explanation.walkthrough: SPINE, backbone or strength of character, loses its last letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Spin is the slanted presentation of news by politicians and their advisers.

clue.text: Reasonably good string playing interrupted by song by man

indicators.note: interrupted by says the fiddling word is broken into by the next pieces

parts.note: fiddling is playing the fiddle, a string instrument

indicators.note: by here means next to, so the song word sits beside the man

parts.note: an air is a tune or song
a tom is a male, as in tomcat

explanation.surface: A violinist's playing is cut short by a man singing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'interrupted by' puts AIR and TOM after the F of FIDDLING.
explanation.definitionFit: Fair to middling is an idiom for moderately good, so-so.

clue.text: Time line incorporates enthusiastic journey

indicators.note: incorporates means takes in, so the two letters take in the enthusiastic word

parts.note: a rave review is an enthusiastic one

explanation.surface: A timeline that includes a keen trip.
explanation.definitionFit: To travel is to make a journey from one place to another.

clue.text: Irritable servants will appear in it

definitions.meaning: bad-tempered, as if from a disordered liver
the uniform worn by household servants

explanation.surface: Ill-tempered servants about to make an appearance.
explanation.definitionFit: Livery means peevish, like liverish, and is also the uniform of servants.

clue.text: Fine diatribe keeping newspaper in good odour?

indicators.note: keeping means holding, so fine and the diatribe together hold the newspaper

parts.note: F is the pencil-grade abbreviation for fine
a rant is a diatribe
a rag is a low-grade newspaper

explanation.surface: A rant that keeps a newspaper in favour.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in good odour' usually means in favour; here it means sweet-smelling.
explanation.definitionFit: Fragrant means sweet-smelling, having a pleasant scent.

clue.text: Something that's played up, causing dangerous situation

indicators.note: up in a down answer means the word is read from bottom to top

parts.note: an actor plays a part

explanation.surface: Something that's acting up and putting someone in peril.
explanation.walkthrough: 'played up' suggests misbehaving, but 'up' reverses PART.
explanation.definitionFit: A trap is a snare, any situation that catches someone unawares.

clue.text: Ask identified person to appear in comic vein

indicators.note: to appear in says the person goes inside the shuffled letters
comic means funny or absurd, so the letters are jumbled

parts.note: in a game of tag the chosen chaser is it

explanation.surface: Asking a known person to turn up in a playful mood.
explanation.walkthrough: 'comic' shuffles VEIN to INVE, and 'to appear in' puts IT inside.
explanation.definitionFit: To invite someone is to ask them to come.

clue.text: Moonshine upset hard drinker

indicators.note: upset in a down answer turns the letters upside down, reading backwards

parts.note: H is the pencil-grade abbreviation for hard
a sot is a drunkard

explanation.surface: Illicit liquor upsets a heavy drinker.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Moonshine' means nonsense here, not bootleg spirit.
explanation.definitionFit: Tosh is nonsense, and moonshine also means foolish talk.

clue.text: Flight highpoint between mid-West and East

indicators.note: between says the high point sits between the other two pieces
mid means the middle letters of the word that follows

parts.note: a cap is a top or high point

explanation.surface: An aircraft route peaking between the Midwest and the East.
explanation.definitionFit: A flight from danger is an escape, a getaway.

clue.text: Saw a source of colours for use around house

indicators.note: around says the prism word goes round the house abbreviation

parts.note: a prism splits white light into a spectrum of colours

explanation.surface: Instructions for a saw, a rainbow source for use around the home.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Saw' is a noun meaning a saying, not a tool.
explanation.definitionFit: A saw is an old saying, a maxim, just as an aphorism is a pithy statement.
